It is also a settled legal principle that fresh claims set up during the appeal proceedings which are in total variance to the original pleadings before the Commission and the memorandum of appeal, do not merit any consideration and are liable to be rejected straightaway. _38._ Vide order dated 04.03.2024, this Tribunal had directed the appellant to file an affidavit stating as to which of its claims does it intend to give up. Neither had the appellant sought permission to agitate any fresh claim/Change in Law event nor was any such permission given by this Tribunal. The conduct of the appellant in setting up fresh claims with regards _42._ Arguments had been advanced by the learned senior counsels for the parties on two more aspects namely (a) whether the claim of the appellant in respect of Change in Law events now sought to be agitated by way of affidavit dated 25.03.2024 are within limitation and (b) whether the Change in Law notices dated 28.12.2017 and 28.06.2018 issued by the appellant are in respect of these Change in Law events also? Once we have held that the Change in Law events sought to be agitated by the appellant by way of affidavit dated 15.03.2024 are not only beyond the scope of this appeal but also _de hors_ the pleadings of the parties before the Commission and thus, do not merit any consideration, we do not find it appropriate to discuss these two aspects. We leave these two aspects to be decided by the Commission in a fresh petition to be filed by the appellant, if so advised, to claim relief with regards to the Change in Law events related to captive coal block. Any discussion by us on these two aspects in this judgment may prejudice the case of either of the parties in the proceedings to be initiated by the appellant in future, if any.
